description:
Channel registry (web, POS, presale, reseller) with per-channel price/fee rules and sales windows; presale/unlock codes; external reseller API selling from shared inventory.

**Conditions of Success:**
- A channel = allocation + price/fee rules + window, all overridable per TKT-5 hierarchy
- Presale codes gate access to configured windows
- Reseller API sells from shared inventory with the same no-oversell guarantee and per-reseller attribution

Lineage: docs/product/brief.md · docs/product/prd-v1.md (capability map).

comments.body: COS defined at epic level. Not yet decomposed — US-stories are created when the owner prioritizes this epic (Gate 1), per PRD 'Capability map'.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### ⚠️ Decomposition readiness — CONCERNS

Decomposed into six vertical slices (TKT-235 … TKT-240), ordered by dependency.

| Child | Slice | Blocked by |
|---|---|---|
| TKT-235 | US-CH1 Channel registry (catalog table + CRUD + reads) | — |
| TKT-236 | US-CH2 Back-office channel + allocation administration | 235 |
| TKT-237 | US-CH3 Per-channel price rules (the axis fees already have) | 235 |
| TKT-238 | US-CH4 Per-channel sales windows (claim-time, clock_timestamp()) | 235 |
| TKT-239 | US-CH5 Presale unlock codes (gated-channel access) | 235, 238 |
| TKT-240 | US-CH6 Reseller API (partner identity + seam closure) | 235, 237, 238 |

**What was already shipped, and therefore is not in scope here:** channel allocations with caps and scheduled release (TKT-78 / ADR-024), per-channel *fee* rules (TKT-214 / ADR-046) and per-channel split schedules (TKT-216 / ADR-047). Each of those tickets deferred the registry, pricing, windows and reseller work to TKT-17 by name; this decomposition is the redemption of those deferrals.

| Criterion | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Sizing | ✅ | Six slices, each end-to-end and independently demoable; none is a horizontal layer |
| Prefactoring split out first | ✅ | TKT-235 (registry) is the prefactor; everything else hangs off it |
| Ordered by dependency | ✅ | No forward dependencies; cycle check walked — none |
| AC verifiable | ✅ | Every COS names a test or an observable refusal |
| Dependencies wired | ✅ | `blocked-by` links set on 236, 237, 238, 239, 240 |
| Context-mémo baked | ✅ | Per child, `governingAdrs` populated from docs/adr/ by area; every cited ADR verified to resolve at HEAD |
| Quality gates | ✅ | `make check` on all; `make browser` additionally on TKT-236 (web-UI write forms) |
| No unvalidated assumption | ⚠️ | See concerns 1–3 |

**Concerns:**
1. **TKT-240 introduces a third identity class** (machine-to-machine partner credential) on an externally reachable surface. ADR-043 decides *where* the guard lives; the credential *shape* is an open design decision that would normally be `owner: human` and hold at Gate 1.
2. **TKT-240 closes the commerce→inventory channel seam, which is an intended breaking change** — some reserves that succeed today will return 409. It is documented as deliberate at `services/commerce/internal/api/server.go:260-263`, so closing it is a product decision, not a defect fix.
3. **TKT-237 and TKT-239 touch money and the contention hot path** respectively, with data migrations on both.

**Verdict:** CONCERNS — structurally sound and ready to run, with three named risks concentrated in TKT-237/239/240. Under normal operation this verdict asks the owner to clear Gate 1 eyes-open. On this run the owner has explicitly waived the gates and reaffirmed after being shown concerns 1–3 by name; the children proceed on that waiver, and every objection overridden downstream is recorded in each child's `kind=metrics` `overrides:` list.
